newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lehman downgrades LVMH after DFS news.
newsitem.headline: Lehman downgrades LVMH after DFS news.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said on Friday it downgraded LVMH to "neutral" from "outperform", questioning the luxury group's decision to purchase U.S. duty free chain DFS.
In a research note analyst John Wakely said LVMH was investing in a new sector, retailing, where it had "no special skills".
He also said that whatever the short- term financial merits of the deal, it "will surely lead investors to question what sort of company LVMH is".
Although earnings growth of LVMH in the short run will not be impacted by the deal, the move may raise questions on LVMH's "not exactly low" valuation, he aded.
"We believe the stock is dead money for the time being until a clearer indication of this company's strategy becomes apparent," he said
Wakely however stressed that LVMH's "underlying earnings momentum was "quite good".
He said the luggage business should show positive volume growth in the second half 1996 and for 1997,
Volume growth in cognac is close to double digits though weakness of the yen will hurt in 1997, he said
Champagne demand is soaring and perfumes are "not as bad as the firt half might suggest,"
